% Generated by task tex-obligations from dossiers/obligations.md (its sections 1 to 5): the
% hierarchy of proof obligations, the error composed, the validation of the two outlines, and
% the findings the tree reveals. Node numbers are the dossier's.
% Breakable inline code for tables (LuaLaTeX), the same definition as the boundary fragments'.
\ifdefined\bndc\else
\directlua{
  bndbreak = function(s)
    local bs = string.char(92)
    local hash = string.char(35)
    s = s:gsub(hash .. hash, hash)
    local after = { ["."] = true, ["_"] = true, ["/"] = true, [":"] = true, [","] = true,
      ["-"] = true, [")"] = true, ["]"] = true, ["="] = true, ["|"] = true }
    local prev = ""
    for _, c in utf8.codes(s) do
      local ch = utf8.char(c)
      if ch:match("^[A-Z]$") and prev:match("^[a-z]$") then
        tex.sprint(bs .. "penalty400{}")
      end
      tex.sprint(-2, ch)
      if after[ch] or c > 127 then
        tex.sprint(bs .. "allowbreak{}")
      end
      prev = ch
    end
  end
}
\newcommand{\bndc}[1]{\texttt{\directlua{bndbreak("\luaescapestring{\detokenize{#1}}")}}}
\fi

\section{The shape of the tree}\label{sec:obl-shape}

\textbf{Sources and revisions.} The tree was drawn by the review\'s task \code{obligations} on 2026-09-30. Object: leanerVM \code{main} at \code{b435631} (every Lean citation at that revision, \code{git show b435631:<path>}); ground truth leanVM at \code{a386121f} (read with \code{git -C /home/scaraven/Documents/leanEthereum/leanVM show a386121f:<path>}; the checkout has moved, brief §8); libraries at the old pins (ArkLib \code{dca90385}, CompPoly \code{3468b38c}, VCVio \code{f9dc47d9}, Clean \code{93c9d1ef}) unless the new pin (\code{7653a901}, \code{572f9973}, \code{a4232d08}, \code{42fe4b26}) is named. No Lean was run for this dossier: every status below rests on the sibling dossiers' recorded probes (named at each node) or on reading the sources.

Inputs, read in the order the task gave: \code{docs/architecture.md} and \code{docs/roadmap/protocol-blueprint.md} at \code{b435631}; the dossiers \code{code-spine}, \code{lib-arklib}, \code{gt-bus}, \code{gt-table-pub}, \code{gt-flock-ring}, \code{code-pubinput}, \code{boundary-adaptor}, \code{literature}, \code{code-layer1}, \code{gt-opening-compile} (complete when read: its summary is headed ``Conclusions'' with five items and its sections A to G are written), \code{lib-others}, and the \code{register} staging (its row identifiers are quoted in parentheses only where they locate a finding); the Lean sources of \code{LeanerVM/Protocol/} at \code{b435631} for every name.

Abbreviations for pointers: \code{bp:NNN} is a line of the blueprint at \code{b435631}; \code{arch:NNN} a line of \code{docs/architecture.md} at \code{b435631}; a dossier is named by its task name and section.

\textbf{What was examined.} The two existing outlines (\code{docs/architecture.md}'s T4 and its obligation map; the blueprint's holes table and Layers 0 to 13) and, through the review's dossiers, what leanVM at the pin actually runs, what ArkLib and the other libraries prove and admit, and what is built at \code{b435631}. From these the complete hierarchy of proof obligations was written (\cref{sec:obl-tree}): the tree whose root is the pair of Layer 13 theorems, whose next level is the compiled verifier's theorems, then the master theorems of the oracle protocol, then the six phases' completeness and knowledge-soundness obligations, then the generic components each is built from and the helper statements each needs, down to the library facts; beside it the adaptor's obligations (2.6) and the table of hypotheses discharged by verifier checks or by conditions on public data (2.7). \Cref{sec:obl-error} composes the errors; \cref{sec:obl-outlines} validates the two outlines against the tree; \cref{sec:obl-findings} states what the tree reveals that no sibling dossier says.

\textbf{The shape of the tree.} 155 numbered nodes in seven tiers (2.0 the root, 2.1 the compiled verifier, 2.2 the master theorems and the spine, 2.3 the phases, 2.5 the generic components and the layers below the phases, 2.6 the adaptor and leanISA, 2.7 the hypotheses table), with up to four numbered levels inside a tier (22 nodes at the first level, 80 at the second, 53 at the third and fourth; 152 carry a status, the other three are a group header and two pointers). Seven arrows carry the error from the phases to the deployed claim (\cref{sec:obl-error-ni}, \cref{tab:obl-arrows}): the spine's per-challenge composition (built), the list-binding compilation (not stated), Theorem B.7 (specified), round-by-round to state-restoration (commented out upstream), the Merkle interface with its hash term (empty as stated), the chain lemma (not stated), the grinding model (no theorem exists), and the family composition over the prover's sizes (not stated).

Nodes on which the review found the blueprint's statement wrong, missing or unprovable: 57 (wrong 22, missing 26, unprovable 9). Every built theorem (the spine, the public-input phase, Layer 1, the ported append, the counting bounds) rests on the kernel's three standard axioms; no admitted library theorem is in its closure (lib-arklib B.1; code-spine P1; probes-rerun 1.0 at the new pin). A node marked \oblreview{…} is one on which the review found the blueprint's statement wrong, missing or unprovable; the tag says which. In the tree (\cref{sec:obl-tree}) such a node carries a leading \oblflag mark.

\textbf{The trusted leaves} (what a reader of the planned chain must accept, today and after every hole is filled as planned; the nodes are 2.1.1.3, 2.1.2.1, 2.1.2.2, 2.1.2.4.1, 2.1.2.4.11, 2.1.2.6, 2.1.2.7, 2.1.5, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.3.2, 2.3.3.5, 2.3.4 (whole), 2.3.4.3.2, 2.3.4.6, 2.5.6.4, 2.5.7.4, 2.6.1, 2.6.2.5, 2.6.2.6, 2.6.3, and the four unbuilt phases' bundles):

\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item \emph{Assumed interfaces:} \code{FiatShamirSecurity} (false as stated, 2.1.2.1), \code{BcsSecurity} (empty as stated, 2.1.2.2), \code{McaJohnson} (2.1.2.4.1), the Flock phase's definition, completeness and security (\code{FlockInterface}, 2.3.4), the witness generator \code{FlockWitnessGen} with its lemma (2.6.3), and, until every hole is filled, the \code{Complete} and \code{Security} fields of the bus, table, Flock and opening phases (2.3).
\item \emph{Admitted upstream theorems the plan consumes:} [BCHKS25] Theorem 4.6 (\code{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range}, a preprint with a sketched proof); the round-by-round to plain implication, if the plain corollary is stated (2.1.2.7). The sumcheck's admitted completeness and knowledge soundness (2.5.1.2, 2.5.1.3) and ArkLib's admitted append (2.2.2.1) are replaced by local proofs in the plan and are not leaves.
\item \emph{Hypotheses nothing discharges:} the random-oracle heuristic for BLAKE2s's compression and its collision resistance (2.1.5); \code{WellFormedBytecode prog} (absent from Layer 13's statements; 2.7); the resource bound on the trace and the constructed witness that \code{baseProver_complete} needs (2.7); the success of the honest grind (2.1.4); the carrier of ``the R1CS with the constant position holds \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} the limb slots compress'' (2.6.2.5); the \code{F_2}-independence of Flock's 128 fixed equality weights (2.3.4.3.2, true by a probe, in no theorem); the oracle-freeness of the front phases (2.1.2.3.3, \cref{f:obl-oracle-free-front}); a bound on \code{piopError} (2.2.2.5); \code{s.Admissible prog} at the adaptor (2.6.2.6, discharged by the verifier's setup check once \code{Admissible} has the two windows).
\item \emph{Transcribed data whose only check is a fixture:} the leanISA instance (layouts, separators, count columns, boundary blocks, lines, the tie order of equal-size blocks, the leaf stacks' order; 2.6.1, 2.5.6.4, 2.3.1.3.8), the WHIR parameters and Merkle formats (2.1.2.4.11, 2.1.2.6, 2.1.1.3), Flock's circuit and constants including \code{R1CS_DIGEST} (2.3.4.6), the scalar oracle interfaces (2.5.7.4), and the fact that the phases' definitions are leanVM's (2.2.2.6: no theorem of the oracle protocol says so; \code{verify_iff_compiled} with its fixture and the review of each \code{Def} do).
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{The error, composed} (\cref{sec:obl-error}). Per challenge, the review finds the blueprint's charges right and tight for \code{ξ} (\code{(B+2)/|E|}), the table rounds (\code{3/|E|}), \code{r} (\code{1/|E|}), \code{λ} (\code{(J−1)/|E|}) and \code{(α, β)} (\code{4·2^{μ_bus}/|E|}, within a factor 2); wrong for the GKR rounds (\code{4/|E|}, not \code{5/|E|}), the last combiner and the binary layer's challenge; charged three incompatible ways for the recycled zerocheck point, which adds nothing; and describing rounds that do not exist for the opening (WHIR's own rounds carry \code{2L_i/|E| + 2^{ℓ_i−j}a_i/|E|}). The interactive error of the oracle protocol is about \code{2^{-159.7}} under the stacking window, dominated by ring switching's \code{2^{32}/|E|}; the blueprint's \code{piopError_le} is false at the per-log caps and true under the window. After Fiat–Shamir the governing quantity is the largest per-challenge error of the compiled protocol, set by WHIR's query rounds (\code{2^{-111}} before 17 bits of grinding) and folds (\code{2^{-128.2}}), not by anything in the oracle protocol; the blueprint's \code{niError = Q · max_i ε_i} lacks the list-size factor \code{L_0} on every front challenge, the hash-collision term, a model of grinding (without which it certifies about 111 bits), the family composition over the announced sizes and the program-hash term.

\textbf{Findings by severity} (\cref{sec:obl-findings}): \emph{major} — twenty-one obligations of the composition have no hole, layer or owner (\cref{f:obl-unowned}); the compilation needs every phase before the opening to make no oracle query, and nothing states or enforces it (\cref{f:obl-oracle-free-front}). \emph{Minor} — the per-challenge error has no carrier for the grinding bits (\cref{f:obl-grinding}). \emph{Note} — the smallest set of unbuilt nodes that makes the master theorems about leanVM (\cref{f:obl-smallest-set}).

\textbf{Validation of the outlines} (\cref{sec:obl-outlines}): \code{docs/architecture.md}'s T4 has the right decomposition and the right headings, gets the shape of the base theorem wrong (a probability attached to a closed Boolean, the defect the blueprint transcribes), drops \code{WellFormedBytecode} at T4, and lacks the list-binding compilation, the grinding model and the family composition; its completeness dual (T2 with the honest prover, resource conditions recorded) is right and the blueprint diverges from it. The holes table covers what it names, with the corrections of \cref{sec:obl-holes} per row, and omits the twenty-one units of \cref{f:obl-unowned}.

\textbf{Not done, and what would verify it.} No Lean was run: every status rests on the sibling dossiers' recorded probes or on reading; the counts are by the first status tag of each node (a node may carry two). The per-challenge errors were taken from the dossiers that worked them (gt-bus D.3, gt-table-pub D, gt-flock-ring 5.2, gt-opening-compile F) and checked for consistency between them, not re-derived. The value of \code{L_0} at production parameters is the opening dossier's reproduction of the Rust's search (110 to 396 at level 0), not a run of the Rust's \code{validate()}.


\section{The tree}\label{sec:obl-tree}

How to read it. The root is what the proof system must deliver to the rest of the verification: the two theorems of the blueprint's Layer 13, which are the proof-system half of target T4 (\code{arch:261-275}). Each level below is what the level above consumes. A node has: a name (and the Lean name the blueprint or the code gives it), what it states for a zkVM engineer, which node(s) it feeds, its status tag, and where the review's dossiers speak about it. The tree is written for the proof system as the blueprint plans it, with the review's corrections marked in place; the adaptor (Layer 3) and leanISA's theorems are a separate branch (2.6), and the hypotheses discharged by verifier checks or by conditions on public data are collected in a table at the end (2.7).

One convention: ``the front'' names the oracle protocol's phases before the opening, \code{commit ⟫ bus ⟫ table ⟫ pub ⟫ flock}; ``the pool'' is the list of claims those phases leave for the opening.

Each node is shown as the dossier writes it: its number and name in bold; in parentheses the Lean name and the lines that state it; what it states for a zkVM engineer; the nodes it feeds; its status tag; and where the review\'s dossiers speak about it (\emph{See}). A leading \oblflag marks a node on which the review found the blueprint\'s statement wrong, missing or unprovable; its \oblreview{\ldots} tag says which. The numbering is the dossier\'s, kept so that the text can refer to a node by its number; the dossier has no tier 2.4.

\subsection[The root (2.0)]{The root (2.0): what the proof system delivers (Layer 13, the proof-system half of T4)}\label{sec:obl-tier-root}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.0.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.0.1 Base extraction} (\lean{baseVerifier_extractsExecution}, \code{bp:1247-1248}; \code{arch:264-269}). \emph{States:} an adversary that makes the executable verifier \code{verify prog input proof} accept yields, except with probability \code{niError}, a stack whose rebuilt witness satisfies leanISA's relation, hence an execution of the program on the public input. \emph{Feeds:} T4, T7 through T5 and T6 (recursion consumes the extracted witness). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{unprovable as written} \oblreview{wrong} — as sketched it has no probability space (its hypothesis is a closed Boolean), concludes an existential (soundness, not knowledge), names no adversary or query budget, and drops \code{WellFormedBytecode prog}, which \code{constraintSoundness} needs; the well-formed statement is a bound on the event ``\code{verify^H} accepts and the extracted stack has no execution'' over a random oracle \code{H}, for a \code{Q}-query adversary, under \code{WellFormedBytecode}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.1; boundary-adaptor findings 3 and 16, E.6; docs-debt (DD1). \emph{Consumes:} 2.1.2 (knowledge soundness of \code{verify}), 2.6.2 (the adaptor's soundness bridge), 2.6.6 (\code{constraintSoundness}), 2.1.5 (the random-oracle heuristic, non-formal).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.0.2}\oblflag\textbf{2.0.2 Base completeness} (\lean{baseProver_complete}, \code{bp:1249-1250}; \code{arch:273-275}). \emph{States:} from a valid execution (with fill blocks in the program), the honest Lean prover's proof is accepted by \code{verify}. \emph{Feeds:} T4's completeness half, T8. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{unprovable as written} \oblreview{unprovable} — false without a resource hypothesis (a valid execution with \code{κ_mem = 32} has a stack above \code{2^28}, which the verifier rejects), and ``the witness of \code{t}'' needs a witness generator (T2, out of scope) or a classical choice; the honest prover's grinding search makes \code{prove} partial, so the equation must be \code{prove … = some proof → verify … = true}. \emph{See:} boundary-adaptor finding 4, C (rows ``resource bound'', ``constructed witness''); gt-opening-compile E.5; docs-debt (DD19). \emph{Consumes:} 2.6.7 (\code{constraintCompleteness}), 2.6.3 (\code{m3Holds_stackOf}), 2.2.1 (\code{piop_perfectCompleteness}), 2.1.4 (completeness through the compilation), 2.1.6 (the prover's grind).
\end{itemize}
