\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.1.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.1.1 Round-by-round to state-restoration knowledge soundness.} \emph{States:} the per-round errors bound a state-restoration adversary's success by \code{(t + k) · max_i ε_i}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing} — commented out in ArkLib with the wrong error (\code{Implications.lean:230-254}); not in the blueprint's interface list. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.2 (last bullets); lib-arklib D.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.1.2}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.1.2 The hash chain is as good as the ideal per-round challenge oracle.} \emph{States:} the ratcheted BLAKE2s chain with its four tags and fixed-width blocks loses at most a collision term against the oracle keyed by the whole prefix; the encoding is injective. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} literature E.6 (LT10), G.3 (transcript-encoding advisories); gt-opening-compile E.2 (c).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.1.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.1.3 The grinding model.} \emph{States:} a query to \code{H} at a ground round costs \code{2^{b_i}} queries in expectation, so the effective error of that round is \code{2^{-b_i} ε_i}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}; no theorem in the literature for multi-round IOPs. \emph{See:} literature A.3 item 3, G.5 (LT13); gt-opening-compile D.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.1.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.1.4 The hash-collision term.} \emph{States:} \code{3.5 t²/2^256} (or \code{3(Q²+1)/2^256}) for the chain and the trees. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} literature A.3 item 2 (LT3).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.1.5}\textbf{2.1.2.1.5 Program binding through its hash.} \emph{States:} two programs with the same \code{bytecode_hash} share every challenge; the statement binds the program up to a BLAKE2s collision, a term of \code{niError}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.1.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.1.6}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.1.6 The family composition over the prover's sizes.} \emph{States:} \code{verify} dispatches on eight announced sizes; a bound per admissible \code{s} transfers to the union only with an argument on how the adversary's queries split among members, and \code{niError} must be uniform in \code{s} or take the maximum. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} boundary-adaptor B.3, finding 6; gt-opening-compile E.1.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.2}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.2 Merkle (BCS) security interface} (\lean{BcsSecurity}, \code{bp:1225}). \emph{States, as the blueprint has it:} ``Merkle-compiled oracles: extraction from collision resistance / ROM''. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, assumed interface} \oblreview{wrong} — names a property with no error and no object; to be true and strong enough: the Merkle compilation of \code{pcs/merkle.rs}, \code{fs/merkle.rs} (leaf = BLAKE2s of the row image, node = BLAKE2s of two children, height and leaf width fixed from public data) preserves state-restoration knowledge soundness in the random-oracle model with the straight-line extractor reading every committed leaf off the query log, up to \code{3(Q²+1)/2^256}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.2, D.4 (checks M1 to M7); lib-arklib G.4. Its leaves:
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.2.1}\textbf{2.1.2.2.1 Binding of the root to the opened rows} (check M6). \emph{States:} the recomputed root equals the committed one, so the opened rows are the committed ones; without it a total break. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (Layer 11's \code{merkleVerify}). \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile D.4.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.2.2}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.2.2 Role separation of the one BLAKE2s map} (chain block, Merkle node, Merkle leaf, grinding). \emph{States:} no cross-role input is exploitable; replaces domain separation, which the trees lack (fixed height and leaf width do the work, check M7). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} literature E.6 (LT10); gt-opening-compile D.4 (M7), B.4.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.2.3}\textbf{2.1.2.2.3 Straight-line leaf extraction from the query log.} \emph{States:} every leaf the prover can open was hashed, so it is in the log except with the collision or preimage term. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.1.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.2.4}\textbf{2.1.2.2.4 VCVio's Merkle-tree library} (\code{CryptoFoundations/MerkleTree/}, nineteen sorry-free modules at \lean{f9dc47d9}). \emph{States:} a generic Merkle tree with its collision-resistance argument. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin}; fit with leanVM's trees unverified. \emph{See:} docs-debt (DD15).
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.3 The list-binding compilation} (no blueprint name; ``Layer 12 turns list binding into extraction of the one \lean{q}'', \code{bp:1190}; acceptance test 11). \emph{States:} let \code{Front'} be the front with the commit message replaced by an interleaved \code{K}-word \code{w} (the level-0 codeword with position queries) and \code{C := Front' ⟫ whirOpen}; then \code{C} is worst-case round-by-round knowledge sound for \code{M3Rel} with the extractor ``list-decode \code{w}, return the first member satisfying \code{M3Holds}'', with per-challenge errors \code{L_0 · ε_i} at the front's challenges and Theorem B.7's at WHIR's. \emph{Feeds:} 2.1.2; it is where the list-size factor enters \code{niError}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing} — the blueprint assigns the step to \code{verify_knowledgeSound}, whose sketched hypotheses cannot prove it. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.3, G; literature A.3 item 4 (LT2); gt-flock-ring 8.13. Its leaves:
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.3.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.3.1 Every member of the list is \code{K}-valued and of the right size.} \emph{States:} a codeword of the code over \code{E} within radius \code{γ_0 < 1 − √ρ_0} of a \code{K}-valued word is \code{K}-valued (its \code{y} and \code{y²} coordinate projections vanish on more than \code{2^{κ_0} − 1} points), of \code{μ} variables after the level-0 relayout, with zero rows where \code{w} has them. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}; a two-line argument in the dossier, not in the specification. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile G.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.3.2}\textbf{2.1.2.3.2 State functions indexed by a finite set compose by a union bound.} \emph{States:} a knowledge state function ``for every \code{g ∈ Λ(w)}, the front's state at \code{(g, τ)} is false'' escapes with probability at most \code{|Λ(w)|} times the front's worst-case bound; the worst-case form of the spine is what makes this a per-transcript union. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified}; ArkLib has no such lemma. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.3.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.3.3 The front's verifier makes no oracle query.} \emph{States:} every phase before the opening reads the stack only through its extractor, never through a query, so \code{Front'}'s verifier is \code{Front}'s (a cast of \code{OracleReduction}, ArkLib \#383's \code{Cast.lean}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing} — true of the two built phases; nothing states or enforces it for the others (\cref{f:obl-oracle-free-front}). \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.3.4}\textbf{2.1.2.3.4 The seam step.} \emph{States:} the front's \code{toFun_full} in the contrapositive: state false at the front's last transcript implies some pooled claim is false of \code{g}, which is \code{∉ R_open}, Theorem B.7's start invariant. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.3.5}\textbf{2.1.2.3.5 The compiled extractor computes.} \emph{States:} enumeration of the finite code is a definition (Lean has no cost model); efficiency in the literature's sense is Guruswami–Sudan, unnamed. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (acceptance test 24 says ``computable''). \emph{See:} literature A.4 (``computable is not efficient'', LT4), G.2.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4}\textbf{2.1.2.4 WHIR's round-by-round soundness} (\lean{whirOpen_rbrSoundness (mca : McaJohnson)}, \code{bp:1175}; Annex B Theorem B.7, \code{b-polynomial-commitment-scheme.tex:139-152}). \emph{States:} for the relation \code{R_open} (``some codeword within \code{γ_0} of the committed word satisfies every weighted claim''), round-by-round soundness with the per-message errors of Annex B's table; soundness for a language, no extractor named. \emph{Feeds:} 2.1.2.3. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; a Lean proof would be the first machine-checked proof of this variant. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.5, B.6; literature C.3. Its leaves:
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.1}\textbf{2.1.2.4.1 Mutual correlated agreement up to the Johnson bound} (\lean{McaJohnson}, \code{bp:1176}; ArkLib \lean{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range}, \code{CapacityBounds.lean:203-219}). \emph{States:} [BCHKS25] Theorem 4.6 as printed (with \code{m = max(⌈√ρ/(1−√ρ−δ)⌉, 3)} and the reduced rate), for the affine line, converted to the fold in characteristic two by Annex B's footnote. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{admitted upstream} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, assumed interface} — a preprint theorem with a sketched proof; the only coding-theoretic input. \emph{See:} literature C.2, C.4 (LT7, LT8); gt-opening-compile E.2; lib-arklib B.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.2}\textbf{2.1.2.4.2 The Johnson bound} (Annex B \code{B:391-414}). \emph{States:} the list within radius \code{γ_i < 1 − √ρ_i − η_i} has at most \code{L_i = 1/(2η_i√ρ_i)} members. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (proved in the annex, not in Lean). \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.5, F.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.3}\textbf{2.1.2.4.3 Folding preserves lists} (Lemma B.10, \code{B:189-198}, with the \lean{2^{ℓ−1}} row union). \emph{States:} the fold of a word close to a list is close to the folded list, except with the MCA error times the row union. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.4}\textbf{2.1.2.4.4 Out-of-domain separation} (Lemma B.11, \code{B:200-206}; check W2). \emph{States:} after the OOD sample the new oracle's list has at most one member consistent with the transcript, except with \code{C(L_i, 2)·μ_i/|E|}; without OOD binding the query phase would pay a union over the list. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile D.5 (W2), F.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.5}\textbf{2.1.2.4.5 Per-level batching} (check W4). \emph{States:} the level's claims (OOD first, queries after, running claim at \code{λ_i^0}) settle in one identity, error \code{(J_i − 1)L_i/|E|}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile D.5 (W4).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.6}\textbf{2.1.2.4.6 The fold rounds.} \emph{States:} each of the \code{ℓ_i} sumcheck rounds of level \code{i} costs \code{2L_i/|E| + 2^{ℓ_i−j} ε_i} (the running claim is a cofactor with \code{c_1} derived, as in the table sumcheck). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; the blueprint's Layer 10 ``2/\textbar{}E\textbar{} per round'' is the tail's value, wrong for these. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.6.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.7}\textbf{2.1.2.4.7 The query rounds} (check G1 for the nonce, W3 for row consistency). \emph{States:} \code{t_i} positions sampled after a 17-bit proof of work; error \code{(1 − γ_i)^{t_i} ≈ 2^{-111}} before grinding. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; the grinding is outside every theorem (2.1.2.1.3). \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile D.3, D.5, F.2; literature G.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.8}\textbf{2.1.2.4.8 The terminal check} (W5) and the final plaintext level. \emph{States:} one equation \code{weight · f̃_final(ρ_tail) = t_r} closes the chain; without it nothing is checked about \code{q}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile D.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.9}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.4.9 The column weight of the encoder} (\lean{encode_column_weight}, \code{bp:1170}; Lemma B.14). \emph{States:} position \code{x} of the codeword is an inner product of the message with a weight whose extension the verifier computes in closed form. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — as an existential it is true of any linear map and says nothing about the novel basis; the needed object is the definition \code{columnWeight x} with its closed-form \code{mle} and the equation \code{encode κ R f x = (columnWeight x).pair f}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.6.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.10}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.2.4.10 The encoder} (\lean{encode}, \lean{novelBasis}, \code{bp:1168-1169}; CompPoly's \lean{AdditiveNTT}). \emph{States:} Reed–Solomon encoding in the novel polynomial basis on the additive domain in \code{K}, over \code{K} at level 0 and over \code{E} at every later level. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — \code{encode} over \code{K} alone serves level 0 only. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.6; lib-others B (CompPoly's NTT exists, generic over a basis).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.4.11}\textbf{2.1.2.4.11 The parameters} (\lean{ladder}, \lean{ladder_queries_eq}, the six constants, \code{bp:1155-1165}). \emph{States:} fold factors, rates, query counts and grinding bits per level as \code{whir_config.rs} derives them; \code{(ladder 15 1).map (·.queries) = [223, 55]}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data}; the Python table is reproduced by a scratch port of the Rust's search. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile F.2, B.3 (\code{Level} lacks \code{η}).
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.5}\textbf{2.1.2.5 Perfect completeness of WHIR} (\lean{whirOpen_perfectCompleteness}, \code{bp:1174}). \emph{States:} the honest prover's folds and openings pass every level check. \emph{Feeds:} 2.1.4. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.6.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.6}\textbf{2.1.2.6 Merkle definitions} (\lean{merkleRoot}, \lean{merkleVerify}, \lean{blake2sBytes}, \code{bp:1179-1182}). \emph{States:} BLAKE2s-256 of leaf images and of two-child nodes, the raw path check, the RFC 7693 byte hasher over leanISA's \code{compress}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data}. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile B.4, B.6.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.2.7}\textbf{2.1.2.7 Plain knowledge soundness from the round-by-round form} (ArkLib \lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundness_implies_knowledgeSoundness}, \code{Implications.lean:223-228}). \emph{States:} an interactive prover convinces the verifier without a good first message with probability at most \code{Σ ε_i}. \emph{Feeds:} the blueprint's plain corollary (\code{bp:261}); not needed if 2.1.2.1 consumes the round-by-round form directly. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{admitted upstream}; its transcript-level half is proved by lib-arklib's probe \code{PlainReading} in forty lines; its conclusion forgets the named extractor. \emph{See:} lib-arklib D.1, D.3, G.3; code-spine C.7.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.3 The interactive-oracle form of the compiled protocol} (\lean{leanVmIopp}, \code{bp:1214-1215}). \emph{States:} \code{commit' ⟫ bus ⟫ table ⟫ pub ⟫ flock ⟫ whirOpen}, where \code{commit'} sends the level-0 codeword and \code{whirOpen}'s level-0 batching is the opening phase's \code{λ}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — the blueprint says ``WHIR in place of the evaluation oracle'' after a \code{μ}-round opening sumcheck; see 2.3.5.1. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile A.4, A.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.1.4 Completeness survives the compilation} (\code{bp:1256-1257}: ``without any assumption''). \emph{States:} an honest proof accepted by the interactive verifier on the chain's challenges is accepted by \code{verify} (a statement about two definitions), and the grinding search succeeds. \emph{Feeds:} 2.0.2. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{wrong as written} \oblreview{wrong} — the grind is an unbounded search; in the random-oracle model it fails with probability \code{(1 − 2^{-17})^{2^64}}, and with BLAKE2s fixed its success is a conjecture; \code{prove} must be partial or fuelled. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.5}\textbf{2.1.5 The random-oracle heuristic.} \emph{States:} BLAKE2s's compression function is the random oracle \code{H} of 2.1.2; the theorem about \code{verify} itself is the instantiation of the definitions only. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, hypothesis} — cannot be a Lean hypothesis (false for any fixed function) nor an axiom; must be named in Layer 13 and in \code{docs/architecture.md}; classical (no quantum random-oracle model). \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile E.1; boundary-adaptor C (row ``BLAKE2s as a random oracle''), finding 3; literature B.4 (LT6), G.5 (LT14).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.1.6}\textbf{2.1.6 The honest prover} (\lean{prove}, \lean{leanVmProver}, \code{bp:1145}, \code{bp:1250}). \emph{States:} each phase's prover is a computable function of the witness, the challenges so far and the layer tables; the compiled prover adds encoding, Merkle trees and the grind. \emph{Feeds:} 2.0.2. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (the spine's \code{leanVmProver} is built as the composed prover of whatever bundle is supplied); the phase-level \code{Def}s bundle a real-number error, so on the real protocol neither the verifier nor the extractor compiles (lib-arklib G.5). \emph{See:} lib-arklib G.5 (AK5); code-spine D.5.
\end{itemize}

\subsection[The master theorems (2.2)]{The master theorems of the oracle protocol (2.2; the spine)}\label{sec:obl-tier-master}

Both are one-line proofs of a composed component's own field, stated over an abstract instance \code{I : M3Instance} and a bundle \code{P : Phases I} of five phases with their proofs; they say nothing about leanVM until an instance and leanVM's phases are supplied (code-spine C.4).

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.1}\textbf{2.2.1 Perfect completeness of the oracle protocol} (\lean{piop_perfectCompleteness (P) (C : P.Complete)}, \code{Spine/Compose.lean:162-170}). \emph{States:} for every \code{(input, q)} with \code{M3Holds I input q}, the honest prover and the composed verifier accept with probability one and end in \code{Seam.done} (which is \code{True}). \emph{Feeds:} 2.0.2 through 2.1.4. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (probe \code{P1Axioms} of code-spine; conditional on \code{Phases.Complete}). \emph{See:} code-spine C.4, C.6; lib-arklib E.
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.1.1}\textbf{2.2.1.1 ArkLib's completeness composition} (\lean{OracleReduction.append_perfectCompleteness_of_guarded_verifiers}, \code{Composition/Sequential/OracleCompleteness.lean:54-67}). \emph{States:} two perfectly complete reductions with guarded verifiers, the second complete from every shared-oracle state, compose perfectly; the additive-error form exists too. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin} (probe \code{AxiomsArkLibBuilt}). \emph{See:} lib-arklib E.2, E.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.1.2}\textbf{2.2.1.2 The component-level append} (\lean{Component.Complete.append}, \code{Component.lean:162-169}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}. \emph{See:} code-spine A (catalogue).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.1.3}\textbf{2.2.1.3 The side conditions \code{guarded} and \code{outputPure}} (\lean{Component.Complete}, \code{Component.lean:76-85}). \emph{States:} the verifier is a check followed by a pure verdict; the prover's output makes no oracle query. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition}; both derivable over the empty shared oracle (ArkLib's \code{GuardedForm.ofEmpty}, \code{Prover.instOutputIsPureEmpty}), so \code{outputPure} is redundant. \emph{See:} code-spine finding ``\code{outputPure} is redundant'' (CS5); lib-arklib G.7.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.1.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.2.1.4 Completeness carries no error} (\lean{Component.Complete.complete} is \lean{perfectCompleteness}). \emph{States:} every phase must be perfectly complete; a phase complete up to an error has no place. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition} \oblreview{missing} — ArkLib composes additive completeness errors at both pins; whether Flock needs one is settled by gt-flock-ring (it does not, if the Lean prover sends the true coefficients). \emph{See:} lib-arklib G.2 (AK2); gt-flock-ring 4, 8.4, 8.12.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2}\textbf{2.2.2 Round-by-round knowledge soundness of the oracle protocol} (\lean{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness (P) (S : P.Security)}, \code{Spine/Compose.lean:172-179}). \emph{States:} ArkLib's worst-case round-by-round knowledge soundness of the composed verifier's \code{toVerifier}, from \code{M3Rel I} to \code{Seam.done I}, for the named extractor \code{piopExtractor P S} and the composed knowledge state function, at the per-challenge error \code{piopError P}: for every statement, every prefix and every challenge index, the probability over one uniform challenge that the state goes from false to true is at most the error of that challenge. \emph{Feeds:} 2.1.2.3 (through the list-binding compilation), 2.1.2.7. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (probes \code{P1Axioms}, \code{AxiomsLeanerVM}; conditional on \code{Phases.Security}). \emph{See:} code-spine C.4, D.3; lib-arklib D.1, D.2 (adequacy of the notion).
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2.1}\textbf{2.2.2.1 The knowledge-soundness append for a guarded first verifier} (\lean{Verifier.append_rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith_of_guarded_first}, \code{ToArkLib/KnowledgeAppend.lean:510}; the port of ArkLib \#615). \emph{States:} two worst-case round-by-round knowledge-sound verifiers, the first guarded, append to one with the appended extractor and each challenge keeping its own error. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (diffed line by line against \#615's file). \emph{See:} lib-arklib C.1, C.2; ArkLib's own \code{append_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} is \oblstatus{major}{admitted upstream} at both pins (ledger A2), and \#615 is open and in conflict on a framework upstream calls legacy (lib-arklib G.3).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2.2}\textbf{2.2.2.2 The appended knowledge state function} (\lean{Verifier.KnowledgeStateFunction.appendGuarded}, \code{KnowledgeAppend.lean:474}). \emph{States:} the first component's state until its verdict, then the second's, with the seam round handled (\code{backward_right}, \code{extractMid_seam}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}. \emph{See:} lib-arklib C.2, G.9.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2.3}\textbf{2.2.2.3 ArkLib's extractor append} (\lean{Extractor.RoundByRound.append}, \code{Append/StateFunction.lean:75}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin}. \emph{See:} lib-arklib B.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.2.2.4 The composed extractor} (\lean{piopExtractor P S}, \code{Compose.lean:153}; \lean{commitExtractor}, \lean{Component.sendExtractor}, \code{SendOracle.lean:134}). \emph{States:} the commit phase's extractor reads the stack off the first message; the phases' extractors (all with witness \code{Unit}) are appended through the verdicts; the chain is computable (\code{isNoncomputable = false}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition} \oblreview{missing} — no definition ``the extracted stack'' exists: with a phase that has a round, \code{extractOut} has type \code{Unit} and the stack is \code{extractMid} at round 0, so acceptance test 24's \code{rfl} witness is ill-typed (probe \code{P3cExtractor}). \emph{See:} code-spine D.5, finding ``the extracted stack is not a definition'' (CS4); lib-arklib D.6.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2.5}\oblflag\textbf{2.2.2.5 A bound on the composed error} (\lean{piopError P := P.toDef.err}, \code{Compose.lean:149}; the blueprint's \lean{piopError_le}, \code{bp:1130}). \emph{States, as the blueprint has it:} \code{Σ_i piopError s i ≤ 2^40/|E| + flockError} for admissible sizes. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{unprovable as written} \oblreview{unprovable} — the spine's \code{piopError} takes a bundle \code{P}, not sizes \code{s}, and nothing bounds it: five phases that draw a challenge, check nothing and declare error \code{1} inhabit \code{Phases.Security toy} and both master theorems hold of them (probe \code{P4Junk}); the numeric bound is false at the per-log caps (\code{μ_bus = 38} makes the \code{(α, β)} term alone \code{2^40/|E|}) and true with the stacking window, with a margin of about \code{2^8}. \emph{See:} code-spine C.5, D.3 (b), finding ``the declared error is unconstrained'' (CS1); gt-bus D.4, G4; gt-opening-compile F.1.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.2.6}\textbf{2.2.2.6 The phases' definitions are leanVM's.} \emph{States:} nothing in the oracle protocol's theorems pins the phases to leanVM: a zero-round phase whose verifier reads the whole stack through the oracle and decides the seam itself fills every slot at error zero. What pins them is 2.1.1 with its fixture and review of each \code{Def}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data} (as a fact about the design). \emph{See:} code-spine D.3 (d); gt-table-pub E.4 item 6 (TP13).
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.3}\textbf{2.2.3 The relation and the seams} (built definitions the theorems are about).
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.3.1}\textbf{2.2.3.1 The relation on the stack} (\lean{M3Holds I input q}, \code{Spine/Instance.lean:219-220}; \lean{M3Rel}). \emph{States:} every constraint polynomial of every table vanishes on that table's rows read out of \code{q}; the pushed and pulled 16-tuples (flush rows and boundary blocks of each side) are the same multiset (\code{List.Perm}, counted in \ensuremath{\N}); every count cell is nonzero; every public line's cells 0 and 1 hold the statement's values; the instance's auxiliary predicate holds. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition}; says what the specification's accept list says, clause by clause, and each clause is refuted alone on the toy (probe \code{P2Relation}). \emph{See:} code-spine C.1, D.1; gt-bus E.5; boundary-adaptor A.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.3.2}\textbf{2.2.3.2 The abstract instance} (\lean{M3Instance}, \code{Instance.lean:119-148}; \lean{Layout}, \lean{Coord}, \lean{BoundaryBlock}, \lean{PublicLine}). \emph{States:} the tables' widths and log-heights, the constraint and flush polynomials with a degree bound \code{d} and its two proofs, the count columns, the boundary blocks, the stack layout with its one reading law, the public lines, the auxiliary predicate. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data} — an instance is data the theorems trust: a layout may alias columns and empty the relation (probe \code{P2Relation}, \code{toyAlias}); only the toy's relation is known inhabited on \code{main}. \emph{See:} code-spine C.2, D.4, finding ``the instance is data the theorems trust'' (CS8); code-layer1 G.10.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.3.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.2.3.3 The seams} (\lean{Seam.commit}, \lean{Seam.bus}, \lean{Seam.table}, \lean{Seam.pub}, \lean{Seam.flock}, \lean{Seam.done}, \code{Spine/Seams.lean:171-191}). \emph{States:} the output relation of each phase is the input relation of the next by definition: \code{M3Holds} of the oracle; then the linear and column claims hold, every term's degree is within \code{d}, the public lines and \code{aux} hold; then column claims, lines, \code{aux}; then column claims and \code{aux}; then column and weighted claims; then \code{True}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition}; each seam inhabited and refuted per conjunct (probe \code{P3aSeams}). \oblreview{wrong} on \code{Seam.bus}: it admits statements the deployed table sumcheck cannot serve (any number of claims, unrelated points, any table, a degree clause on the statement alone), so guards leanVM lacks are forced into the table phase (2.3.2.6). \emph{See:} code-spine C.3, D.2, finding ``the degree conjunct'' (CS2); gt-table-pub E.1, finding ``the bus seam admits statements'' (TP1); gt-bus E.4, G10.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.3.4}\textbf{2.2.3.4 The claim types} (\lean{ColumnClaim}, \lean{VirtualTerm}, \lean{LinearClaim}, \lean{Weight}, \lean{WeightedClaim}, each with \lean{.Holds}, \code{Seams.lean:57-124}). \emph{States:} a column claim is an evaluation of a column at a point through the layout; a linear claim is a weighted sum of extensions of \code{K}-polynomials of one table's rows; a weighted claim is \code{Σ_w W(w)·q(w) = c} with the weight's cube values and its evaluator agreeing. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition}; \code{Weight.onCube} carries \code{2^μ} values no deployed verifier builds (gt-flock-ring 8.16). \emph{See:} code-spine A; gt-opening-compile A.6.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.4}\textbf{2.2.4 The commit phase} (\lean{commitDef}, \lean{commitComplete}, \lean{commitSecurity}, \code{Compose.lean:51-71}; \lean{Component.sendOracle}, \code{SendOracle.lean}). \emph{States:} one prover message, the stack itself, becomes the oracle; the output relation is \code{M3Holds} of the oracle; perfectly complete; knowledge sound at error zero with the extractor that returns the message. \emph{Feeds:} 2.2.1, 2.2.2 (first component of the bundle). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (probe \code{P3bCommit}). ArkLib's own \code{SendSingleWitness.oracleReduction_completeness} is admitted; the local version is justified by the named form. \emph{See:} code-spine D.6; lib-arklib G.8.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.5}\textbf{2.2.5 Transport of knowledge along the adaptor} (\lean{Refinement}, \lean{Refinement.map_option_valid}, \code{ToArkLib/Refinement.lean:31-57}; \lean{Extractor.Straightline.map}). \emph{States:} validity of one extracted witness slot for \code{M3Rel} gives validity of its image under \code{witnessOf} for \code{SatisfiedBy} (pointwise). \emph{Feeds:} 2.0.1. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}; the probabilistic transport, which the blueprint calls unproved and consumer-less, is three lines in the event form (probe \code{P6Surface}, \code{knowledge_transport}) and Layer 13 is its consumer; the lemma has the polarity of the good event where the game needs the bad one (one line to flip); \code{Extractor.Straightline.map} cannot serve (its target witness must be in \code{Type}, and \code{EnsembleWitness} is in \code{Type 1}). \emph{See:} code-spine C.7, D.7, finding ``knowledge transport is three lines'' (CS9); boundary-adaptor E.6, finding 13.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.2.6}\oblflag\textbf{2.2.6 The adequacy of the notion} (ArkLib's \lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith}, \code{Security/RoundByRound.lean:553-569}; \lean{KnowledgeStateFunction}, \code{:164-189}). \emph{States:} what the definition guarantees (lib-arklib D.1) matches the literature's round-by-round knowledge soundness in its worst-case-per-prefix form, with one difference: the extractor may be any function, classical choice included, so the existential forms (\code{rbrKnowledgeSoundness}, \code{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCase}, hence \code{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness_exists}) prove soundness only. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin} as a definition; \oblreview{wrong} for every blueprint interface stated in the existential form (Layer 9's \code{FlockInterface.rbrKnowledgeSoundness}, Layer 10's sketch). \emph{See:} lib-arklib D.2, D.4, D.6, G.1 (AK1); literature A.3 (last paragraph).
\end{itemize}

\subsection[The phases (2.3)]{The phases (2.3): the fields of \texttt{Phases.Complete} and \texttt{Phases.Security}}\label{sec:obl-tier-phases}

Each phase owes three things at its two seams: a definition (\code{Phase.Def}: schedule, prover, verifier, per-challenge error), perfect completeness (\code{Phase.Complete}), and round-by-round knowledge soundness with a named extractor and state function (\code{Phase.Security}). Until every hole is filled, the two bundles are assumed interfaces (\code{bp:1419-1426}): today \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, assumed interface} for the bus, table, Flock and opening phases.


\subsubsection{The bus phase (2.3.1; Layer 6; \texttt{Seam.commit} \texorpdfstring{$\to$}{to} \texttt{Seam.bus})}\label{sec:obl-phase-bus}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.1 Definition} (\lean{busPhase}, \code{bp:955-963}). \emph{States:} the verifier draws \code{(α, β) ∈ E^5}; the prover sends the two roots \code{(R, R_c)} (one root for both bus sides); a combiner \code{λ} after the roots and after every layer (the last drawn and never used); the batched radix-4 GKR over the three fingerprinted product trees (push, pull, count), odd first layer if \code{μ_bus} is odd, ending at one point \code{ζ = (u_0, u_1, χ_0, …)} drawn entirely in the last layer; the check \code{R_c ≠ 0}; the five boundary evaluations; the output is \code{B + 3} linear claims (one per constraint at \code{ζ_{<τ_j}} with value 0; the push, pull and count forms with the derived \code{rem_s}) and five column claims, everything expressible as a \code{BusOut I}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — the sketch has \code{StmtIn := Unit}, a \code{BusOut} with \code{ζ, rem, pool, α, β} the spine does not have, an undefined \code{LeafLayout}, one combiner per layer, and a degree-5 round message where the deployed GKR sends the degree-4 cofactor with \code{c_0} derived and no round check. \emph{See:} gt-bus A.3, A.4, E.1, G1, G2, G8, G11; register (GB1, GB2, GB11).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.2}\textbf{2.3.1.2 Perfect completeness} (\lean{busPhase_perfectCompleteness}, \code{bp:971}). \emph{States:} from \code{M3Holds}: the zerocheck claims hold at every point; the two products are one element; \code{R_c ≠ 0} since every count is nonzero; every layer check passes (no inverse of a challenge); the bus forms hold with the derived \code{rem_s} by the leaf decomposition; the degree conjunct of \code{Seam.bus} by \code{constraints_degree} and \code{flushes_degree}, provided \code{1 ≤ d} whenever there is a count column. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; provable on paper. \emph{See:} gt-bus E.2, G10.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3}\textbf{2.3.1.3 Knowledge soundness} (\lean{busPhase_rbrKnowledgeSoundness … (busError s)}, \code{bp:972}). \emph{States:} one knowledge state function for the whole phase (gt-bus D.3's table): after \code{(α, β)} ``the two products of \code{q}'s leaves are equal and every count is nonzero, the constraints vanish, lines and \code{aux} hold''; after the roots ``\code{R} is both products and \code{R_c} the count product, nonzero''; along the GKR the running claims are the true values; on the last layer's challenges the zerocheck restriction \code{Z(T)} is carried coordinate by coordinate; after the boundary evaluations every output claim holds. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; provable on paper, but not as the blueprint plans it (2.3.1.3.6). \emph{See:} gt-bus D.3, E.2. Its leaves:
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.1}\textbf{2.3.1.3.1 Balance from the product equality} (\lean{sideProduct_collision}, Theorem 5.1; \lean{sideProduct_poly_eq_iff}, Lemma 5.2). \emph{States:} unequal multisets of at most \code{2^μ} 16-tuples give unequal polynomials in \code{K[A_0..A_3, X]} (unique factorization: the factors \code{X − π_A(t)} are monic linear, \code{t ↦ π_A(t)} injective), so they collide at \code{(α, β)} with probability at most \code{4·2^μ/|E|} (total degree 4 in \code{(α, β)}; Schwartz–Zippel). The specification leaves Lemma 5.2's proof \code{TODO}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (Layer 5, hole G4). \emph{See:} gt-bus D.1, E.2; blueprint acceptance test 1; 2.5.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.2}\textbf{2.3.1.3.2 Nonzero counts from \code{R_c ≠ 0}} (check B13). \emph{States:} exact, no probability: the true count product is nonzero iff every count cell is (padding leaves are \code{1}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-bus B (B13), E.2; acceptance test 3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.3}\textbf{2.3.1.3.3 One root, not two} (check B12). \emph{States:} structural: one stream scalar read into both slots; with two roots and no comparison any unbalanced stack passes. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-bus B (B12), G13; acceptance test 4.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.3.4 The GKR's errors} (\lean{gkrError}, \code{bp:941-942}; 2.5.4). \emph{States:} a combiner costs \code{(nside − 1)/|E| = 2/|E|} (a nonzero quadratic in \code{λ}), the last one \code{0}; a layer sumcheck round \code{4/|E|} (two distinct polynomials of degree at most 4 agree at 4 points; the normalized cofactor is what the verifier holds); a combination pair \code{2/|E|} (\code{1/|E|} per coordinate), the binary layer's single challenge \code{1/|E|}; a prover message costs nothing given the layer check. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — the blueprint charges \code{5/|E|} per round (the error of a different verifier that keeps the equality factors), omits the last combiner and the binary layer's challenge. \emph{See:} gt-bus D.3, D.4, G1, G2, G12.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.5}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.3.5 The recycled zerocheck point} (acceptance test 6; row \emph{Seams} \code{bp:333}; \code{bp:1001-1003}). \emph{States:} with the state a conjunction \code{G ∧ Z}, the escape ``some constraint is violated on the cube but every \code{C̃_{j,i}(ζ_{<τ_j}) = 0}'' costs at most \code{1/|E|} per coordinate of \code{ζ} once for all constraints (a multilinear restriction becomes zero for at most one value of the next variable), and the error of a coordinate is the maximum of the GKR's and \code{1/|E|}, that is the GKR's: the recycled point adds nothing to \code{busError}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — charged in the blueprint in three incompatible ways (per coordinate per constraint; \code{τ_max/|E|} per constraint to the \code{(α, β)} and GKR challenges, though \code{(α, β)} precede \code{ζ}; nothing in \code{busError}). \emph{See:} gt-table-pub D.3; gt-bus D.3, G6 (GB6, TP5).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.6}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.3.6 The GKR as a separate component cannot be appended} (\code{bp:930-937}). \emph{States:} Layer 5's \code{gkr} has the leaf tables as its oracles while a phase's one oracle is the stack; carrying the stack along needs ArkLib's \code{liftContext} theorems, admitted at both pins, and an appended state function cannot carry the zerocheck clause that changes with the GKR's challenges. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{unprovable as written} \oblreview{unprovable} — restate the GKR over a context with leaves and riders, or prove the phase with one state function. \emph{See:} gt-bus G3 (GB3); lib-arklib B.3 (ledger A4).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.7}\textbf{2.3.1.3.7 The leaf decomposition} (\lean{leaf_decomposition}, \code{bp:969-970}; Layer 1's \lean{Blocks.stack_eval_ambient_one}, \code{Stack.lean:118}). \emph{States:} the extension of a one-padded leaf stack at \code{ζ} is \code{Σ_b eq(sel_b, ζ_hi)·(β − Σ_i eq(α, i)·c̃_{b,i}(ζ_lo)) + (1 + Σ_b eq(sel_b, ζ_hi))}, equation (2) of §5.4 in characteristic two. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} for the Layer 1 identity (probe \code{ValuesProbe}); the phase-level statement over the leaf layout \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} code-layer1 B.3, A.5; gt-bus A.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.8}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.3.8 The leaf stacks' layout} (the three unowned blocks first; ties by column index). \emph{States:} the order of blocks of equal size decides offsets, selectors and the verdict; \code{M3Instance.tuples} lists flush tuples first, the opposite of the deployed leaf order. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} gt-bus G7 (GB7); code-layer1 G.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.9}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.3.9 Two side conditions on the instance} (\lean{1 ≤ d} with a count column; every table with a constraint has a flush or count on the bus). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}; leanVM's instance meets both. \emph{See:} gt-bus G10 (GB10).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.1.3.10}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.1.3.10 The order of the roots, the boundary evaluations and the linear claims.} \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} gt-bus G8 (GB8).
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The table sumcheck phase (2.3.2; Layer 7; \texttt{Seam.bus} \texorpdfstring{$\to$}{to} \texttt{Seam.table})}\label{sec:obl-phase-table}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.2.1 Definition} (\lean{tableSumcheck}, \lean{tableSummand}, \code{bp:986-990}). \emph{States:} the verifier draws \code{ξ}; constraint \code{i} of table \code{t} takes \code{ξ^{o_t+i}}, the three bus sides \code{ξ^{B+s}} shared by every table; the target \code{Σ_s ξ^{B+s}·rem_s} is derived, never sent; \code{τ_max} rounds (the maximum over the six opcode tables), highest variable first, each with three coefficients \code{c_0, c_2, c_3} on the wire and \code{c_1} derived from the running claim; table \code{t} joins at round \code{τ_max − τ_t} with the weight \code{∏_{m<τ_t}(1+ζ_m+r_m)·∏_{m≥τ_t} r_m} (back-loaded padding); the final message is one value per column of every opcode table (104 for leanVM, the eighteen BLAKE2S limbs included); the final check reproduces the running claim; the claims pooled are the 104 column claims after the five received. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — the sketch's types predate the spine (\code{StmtIn := BusOut} with \code{rem}, \code{StmtOut := BusOut × ColumnClaims}); \code{τ_max} and the final message range over every table of the instance, so with Layer 3's column-only tables the schedule has at least 16 rounds and 110 values where leanVM has \code{τ_max} (as few as 3) and 104; the oracle protocol sends four coefficients and checks the round where the wire carries three and no check (a transport lemma is owed and unstated). \emph{See:} gt-table-pub A.1, C.2, findings ``the table sumcheck's tables are not distinguished'' (TP2), ``the round message'' (TP4), ``Layer 7's sketch'' (TP6); gt-bus G16.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.2}\textbf{2.3.2.2 The target identity} (\lean{tableSummand_target}, \code{bp:991}). \emph{States:} the cube sum of the back-loaded, eq-weighted summand equals \code{Σ_s ξ^{B+s}·rem_s} (the zerocheck claims contribute 0). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; its two Layer 1 ingredients are built: \code{sumCube_padHigh} (\code{Padding.lean:64}, the lift by \code{∏_{k≥τ_j} X_k} keeps the sum) and \code{evalMle_padHigh} (\code{:70}, the extension the verifier's final weight uses). \emph{See:} code-layer1 A.6, B.4, G.9 (acceptance test 7 names the wrong lemma); acceptance tests 7, 9.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.2.3 Perfect completeness} (\lean{tableSumcheck_perfectCompleteness}, \code{bp:993}). \emph{States:} on a statement in \code{Seam.bus} and a stack satisfying it, the honest round polynomials pass and the final values are the true column values. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{unprovable as written} \oblreview{unprovable} — against \code{Seam.bus} as built the deployed sumcheck is not complete (terms of one table at unrelated points need one \code{eq} factor per term; a term on a table taller than \code{τ_max} cannot be folded); provable only for a generalized phase with the guards of 2.3.2.6, or after the seam carries the deployed shape. \emph{See:} gt-table-pub E.1 (a) to (d), E.4.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.4}\textbf{2.3.2.4 Knowledge soundness} (\lean{tableSumcheck_rbrKnowledgeSoundness}, \code{bp:994}; state function of gt-table-pub D.2). \emph{States:} before \code{ξ} every input claim's discrepancy is zero; after \code{ξ} the batching polynomial \code{Σ_c δ_c X^c} vanishes at \code{ξ} (error \code{(k−1)/|E| = (B+2)/|E| = 4/|E|}, tight); after each round the running claim is the true partial sum (\code{3/|E|} per round, tight: two cubics agree at three points); after the final message every column claim holds (no error on a prover message). Back at the bus seam: a false column claim, false lines or \code{aux} are handed on (error 0). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; the two charged terms are correct, tight and on the right challenges. \emph{See:} gt-table-pub D.2, E.3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.5}\textbf{2.3.2.5 The generic sumcheck it rests on} (2.5.1). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} locally; ArkLib's single-round bound \oblstatus{major}{admitted upstream}.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.6}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.2.6 The guards the seam forces} (degree of every term at most \lean{I.d}; at most \lean{B + 3} claims; one point; the tables the sumcheck opens). \emph{States:} ArkLib's round-by-round notion quantifies over every input statement (\code{toFun_empty} is an \code{iff}), so a verifier must reject a statement outside the seam that its checks would otherwise accept: without the degree guard a true cubic claim passes the all-zero run; without the count guard \code{err ξ ≥ (k−1)/|E|} for every \code{k}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing} — the deployed verifiers have no such checks; smallest fix: the shape in the type (\code{BusOut} as the Rust's \code{BusVerify}: one point, forms per side and table with the degree in the type, three totals) or a subtype for the polynomial. \emph{See:} gt-table-pub E.1, finding ``the bus seam admits statements'' (TP1); code-spine C.3, finding ``the degree conjunct'' (CS2).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.2.7}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.2.7 The eighteen limb claims as column claims.} \emph{States:} a limb claim at \code{z} is the claim on \code{q_flock} at \code{(slot bits, z, selector)}; it rests on the layout's reading law (strided low-index selection), which no built layer supplies. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing} (the strided reader, 2.5.6.3). \emph{See:} gt-table-pub E.2; code-layer1 G.1; gt-flock-ring 5.4, 8.2.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The public-input phase (2.3.3; Layer 8; \texttt{Seam.table} \texorpdfstring{$\to$}{to} \texttt{Seam.pub}; built)}\label{sec:obl-phase-pub}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.3.1 Definition} (\lean{publicInputPhase}, \code{PublicInput.lean:376-381}; \lean{pSpec} \code{:99}, \lean{prover} \code{:208}, \lean{verifier} \code{:229}, \lean{check} \code{:136}, \lean{pooled} \code{:127}, \lean{expectedValues} \code{:132}, \lean{lineValue} \code{:119}, \lean{linePoint} \code{:65}). \emph{States:} one challenge \code{r ∈ E}; the prover sends, as one \code{List E}, the values at \code{r} of the lines whose value is sent; the verifier checks the message equals the expected values \code{(1 + r)·cell0 + r·cell1} and rejects otherwise; it pools one claim per line, on the line's column at \code{(r, 0, …, 0)}, with the value it computes, after the received claims. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition}; \code{noncomputable} for its real error only. Faithful to §8.2's per-limb check; \oblreview{wrong} in one respect: the three executable verifiers (Rust, Python, the recursion guest) check one combined equation \code{c_0 + y·c_1 = w_0 + r·(w_0 + w_1)} and pool the scalars sent, and the blueprint assigns their soundness to Layer 12, which can neither state nor detect it. \emph{See:} code-pubinput B.1, A, G.2 (PI2); gt-table-pub F, finding ``the public-input phase proves a check no executable verifier runs'' (TP3).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.2}\textbf{2.3.3.2 Perfect completeness} (\lean{complete}, \code{:300}; \lean{publicInputComplete}, \code{:384}). \emph{States:} from the table seam, for every \code{r}, the honest values pass the check and the pool is in the public seam. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (probe \code{Probe0Baseline}, re-run at the new pin: three standard axioms). \emph{See:} code-pubinput F; probes-rerun 1.0.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.3.3 Knowledge soundness} (\lean{rbr}, \code{:350}; \lean{stateFunction}, \code{:327}; \lean{extractor}, \code{:317}; \lean{publicInputSecurity}, \code{:391}). \emph{States:} worst-case round-by-round knowledge soundness at \code{1/|E|} on the one challenge: outside the table seam, at most one \code{r} puts the pool in the public seam (\code{bad_challenge_unique}); the bound is attained (\code{badLine}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}. \oblreview{wrong} on what it protects: the check on the message is not load-bearing for any theorem of the phase, because \code{pooled} reads the statement, not the message; a verifier that ignores the message has the same \code{Phase.Security} (probe \code{ProbeAnyCheck}, \code{securityG}). The requirement ``a missing check leaves knowledge soundness unprovable'' fails for this check; pooling the values sent, as §8.2 and the deployed verifiers do, restores it. \emph{See:} code-pubinput C.3, C.4, F, G.1 (PI1).
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.3.1}\textbf{2.3.3.3.1 The line identity} (\lean{eval₂Mle_linePoint}, \code{:71}). \emph{States:} the extension at \code{(r, 0, …, 0)} is \code{(1 − r)·q(0) + r·q(1)}; the bit order (coordinate 0 is the low bit) is proved, from Layer 1's \code{evalMle_append_boolVec} at slice zero. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}. \emph{See:} code-pubinput A, negative results.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.3.2}\textbf{2.3.3.3.2 Two distinct lines through \code{K}-cells meet at most once} (\lean{line_challenge_unique}, \code{:152}, private; \lean{bad_challenge_unique}, \code{:186}). \emph{States:} cells differing by \code{(a, c) ≠ 0} are hit when \code{(1 + r)·a + r·c = 0}, one \code{r} at most (\code{ofK} injective, characteristic two). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.3.3}\textbf{2.3.3.3.3 The uniform sampler's law} (\lean{probEvent_uniformSample_le_of_subsingleton}, \code{ToVCVio/UniformSample.lean:44}; \lean{…_of_card_le}, \code{:35}). \emph{States:} an event with at most \code{k} witnesses has probability at most \code{k/|α|} under \code{$ᵗ α}; uniformity is a law of VCVio's \code{SampleableType}, so no instance can be non-uniform. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (probe \code{CountingBounds}); redundant with VCVio's \code{prEvent_uniformSample_le_div_iff} at the new pin. \emph{See:} lib-others E.4, G.10; 2.5.7.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.3.4}\textbf{2.3.3.3.4 The guarded-verdict lemmas} (\lean{Verifier.GuardedForm.of_probEvent_pos}, \code{ToArkLib/GuardedVerdict.lean:40}; \lean{Reduction.mem_support_run_of_guarded}, \code{:73}). \emph{States:} if a guarded verifier can output a statement with a property, its check passed and its verdict has it (the last law of a knowledge state function); every outcome of a run is a prover run plus the verdict. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}; restated on VCVio's new probability API at \code{144c5aa} with the same bounds (brief §8). \emph{See:} code-pubinput A.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.3.5}\textbf{2.3.3.3.5 The verdict as an ordinary verifier} (\lean{verifier_verify}, \code{:253}; \lean{guarded}, \code{:273}; \lean{keepOracles}, \lean{materializeOutput_of_keepOracles}, \code{ToArkLib/KeepOracles.lean}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.3.4 The deployed verifier's phase} (\lean{deployedPhase}, \lean{deployedSecurity}; no blueprint name). \emph{States:} the combined check on the two words with the values sent pooled is knowledge sound at \code{1/|E|}: the words' equation with true claims at two distinct challenges forces the cells and zero top limbs (\code{accepts_two_challenges}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}; key lemma proved in a probe (\code{ProbeWordsLemma}), the full \code{Phase.Security} on paper. \emph{See:} code-pubinput C.13, G.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.3.5}\textbf{2.3.3.5 The top limb} (the third public line \lean{mem_2} with cells \lean{(0, 0)}, \lean{sent = false}). \emph{States:} the claim on \code{mem_2} is pooled with value 0 although no scalar is sent; every theorem of the phase and the spine holds for an instance with two lines; what a missing third line breaks is the adaptor's \code{satisfiedBy_witnessOf} at \code{SatisfiedBy.word0_eq}, whose right-hand side has a zero top limb by the type of \code{PublicInput}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (Layer 3 lists the line; \code{PublicLine.sent} is pinned by prose only). \emph{See:} code-pubinput D, G.3, G.4; boundary-adaptor D; acceptance test 10 (names the wrong witness).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The Flock phase (2.3.4; Layer 9; \texttt{Seam.pub} \texorpdfstring{$\to$}{to} \texttt{Seam.flock}; nothing built)}\label{sec:obl-phase-flock}

Today nothing named \code{FlockInterface}, \code{FlockWitnessGen}, \code{limbColumns} or \code{flockError} exists in Lean; the only instance built has \code{aux := True}, and on it a Flock phase that checks nothing is knowledge sound at error zero (probe \code{NoCheckFlock}). Issue \#3 records ``Flock F0 has not started''. Everything below is \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, assumed interface} for a reader of the master theorems today (gt-flock-ring 7.1).

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.4.1 Definition} (the blueprint's \lean{FlockInterface}, \code{bp:1075-1086}). \emph{States, as deployed:} fifteen steps (gt-flock-ring 2.2): seven fixed equality coordinates, \code{k_batch + 1} sampled ones, the univariate skip (64 values on the coset, \code{z_skip}, the interpolant with 64 assumed zeros), \code{n_flock = 8 + k_batch} zerocheck rounds with \code{c_0} derived, \code{v_a, v_b} with \code{v_c} derived, \code{α_lc}, eight lincheck rounds with \code{c_1} derived, the 64 slice values \code{s_i}, the one check (the lincheck terminal identity with the \code{α³} constant-position term), six ring-switching challenges, the derived target \code{T = Σ_i x^i Φ(s_i)}; the phase reads no claim of the pool and adds one weighted claim on the \code{q_flock} region. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} — Layer 9's interface takes the eighteen limb claims as input and emits one claim, which with leanVM's verifier has knowledge-soundness error 1 (the limb claims stay in the pool and are opened); the spine's slot (\code{FlockOut} with \code{columns} and \code{weighted}) is right. The circuit, wire positions, slot map, \code{g_0}, \code{φ_8} and the floor exist only in the Rust and Python (Category B, no owner). \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 2, 5.1, 5.5, 8.1, 8.7 (FR1, FR7); gt-table-pub finding ``Layer 9's sketch makes the eighteen limb claims an input of Flock'' (TP7).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.2}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.4.2 Perfect completeness} (\lean{FlockInterface.perfectCompleteness}, \code{bp:1083}). \emph{States:} the specification's prover (true coefficients) is accepted at every challenge; no verifier inverts a challenge-dependent value. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} on its obstacle: acceptance test 20 files a completeness failure under \code{flockError}, a soundness error, and attributes to the protocol the inverse \code{(1 + r_eq)^{-1}} only the Rust prover takes (at \code{r_eq = 1} that prover emits a proof its verifier rejects: an implementation defect, probability at most \code{(k_batch + 1)/|E|}). \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 4, 8.4, 8.12 (FR4, FR12); lib-arklib G.2 (AK2, the disagreement is settled gt-flock-ring's way).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.4.3 Knowledge soundness} (\lean{FlockInterface.rbrKnowledgeSoundness … flockError}, \lean{flockError_le}, \code{bp:1084-1085}). \emph{States:} if \code{aux q} fails, the weighted claim is false except with the error; \code{Σ flockError ≤ (4·k_batch + 163)/|E| + 2^32/|E|}, right for a fixed committed polynomial and term by term the Rust's parameters (gt-flock-ring 5.2). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} in form: stated in the existential \code{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCase} (soundness only, 2.2.6) and bundled with completeness (\code{Security extends Complete}). \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 5.2, 8.5 (FR5); lib-arklib G.1. Its leaves:
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3.1}\textbf{2.3.4.3.1 The partially fixed zerocheck} (Annex C.7; \code{03:95-100}). \emph{States:} \code{k_batch + 1} sampled coordinates at \code{1/|E|}; the univariate skip \code{127/|E|} on \code{z_skip} (two polynomials of degree below 128); \code{2/|E|} per quadratic round; \code{1/|E|} more on each of the last \code{k_batch} rounds for the constant position. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3.2}\textbf{2.3.4.3.2 The \code{F_2}-independence of the 128 fixed equality weights.} \emph{States:} the hypothesis of the partially fixed zerocheck holds for the pinned constants. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, hypothesis}; verified by a Python probe (rank 128), asserted by a Rust unit test, stated nowhere in the blueprint. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 5.2, 9.3, 7.1 (row 7).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3.3}\textbf{2.3.4.3.3 The lincheck} (\code{c-flock:112-133}). \emph{States:} \code{3/|E|} on \code{α_lc} (degree three), \code{2/|E|} per round for eight rounds; the terminal identity is the phase's only check, and without it any \code{q_flock} passes. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 3.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.4.3.4 The constant position} (\lean{z(512, t) = 1}; the \lean{α³} term). \emph{States:} without it the all-zero block satisfies the homogeneous R1CS and ``the limb slots compress'' is false. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{missing} — absent from the blueprint's and the docstring's wording of \code{aux}. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 5.3, 8.6 (FR6).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3.5}\textbf{2.3.4.3.5 Ring switching} (Annex A; \code{a-ring:104-128}). \emph{States:} the 64 slice claims at one point reduce to one weighted claim on the packed polynomial through a random \code{F_2}-linear map built from six challenges; no message, no check; error below \code{2^32/|E|} (a nonzero polynomial of total degree \code{2^31 + 2^15 + 2^7 + 2^3 + 2 + 1} in \code{f_0..f_5}); the weight's extension has the closed form \code{Σ_k c_k ∏_n (1 + r_n^{2^k} + r'_n)}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; needs ``\code{x} has 64 distinct conjugates'' and ``the \code{c_k} are distinct monomials'' (Annex A, tested in the Rust); ArkLib's \code{RingSwitching/Packing} is a different protocol (Diamond–Posen), admitted at both pins, and no profile turns it into leanVM's. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 6, 8.9 (FR9); lib-arklib B.3 (ledger A9).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.3.6}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.4.3.6 The auxiliary predicate} (\lean{I.aux}; for leanISA ``Flock's R1CS with the constant position holds of the bits packed into \lean{q_flock}''). \emph{States:} decidable; well defined only from the Rust (the circuit, wire positions and slot map are not in the specification). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{unprovable} as placed: Layer 9 is over an abstract \code{I} whose \code{aux} is opaque and names no column, count or relation, so the Flock phase cannot be written there (a \code{FlockRegion I} supplied by Layer 3 is needed). \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 5.3, 8.3 (FR3); code-spine finding ``the instance is data the theorems trust'' (CS8).
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.4}\textbf{2.3.4.4 The weighted claim's weight is MLE-friendly} (\lean{Weight.mle_eq} for the ring-switched weight). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}, owed by \#3. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 8.16.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.5}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.4.5 The limb columns' slot map} (\lean{FlockInterface.limbColumns}, \code{bp:1077}). \emph{States:} eighteen numbers (\code{hash_flock.rs:87-115}) and a generic low-index selection identity. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{unprovable as written} \oblreview{unprovable} — placed inside an interface that takes the instance as parameter while the instance's layout needs it. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 8.2 (FR2); boundary-adaptor finding 7; code-layer1 G.1.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.4.6}\textbf{2.3.4.6 The constants} (\lean{φ_8}, \lean{0xf7, 0x53, 0xb5}, \lean{g_0}, \lean{R1CS_DIGEST}, the floor \lean{τ_BLAKE2S ≥ 3}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data}; \code{R1CS_DIGEST} cannot be recomputed at the pin and has no owner. \emph{See:} gt-flock-ring 5.5, 8.14 (FR14).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The opening phase (2.3.5; Layer 10; \texttt{Seam.flock} \texorpdfstring{$\to$}{to} \texttt{Seam.done})}\label{sec:obl-phase-opening}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.3.5.1 Definition} (\lean{openingPhase}, \code{bp:1112-1113}). \emph{States, as the blueprint has it:} the verifier draws \code{λ}; a \code{μ}-round sumcheck on \code{W_λ·q}; a final evaluation query of \code{q̃}. \emph{As deployed:} after \code{λ} (drawn after the six ring-switching challenges, every claim value already bound; the ring-switched claim takes \code{λ^0}, the pooled claims the next powers in pool order; \code{J = 113}) the next message is WHIR's first round polynomial; the sumcheck rounds that reduce the weighted claim are WHIR's own, interleaved with its levels, and the protocol ends on one equation, never on an evaluation of \code{q̃} at a point. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{wrong as written} \oblreview{wrong} — a \code{verify} built as written has \code{μ} extra round polynomials, one extra challenge and one extra scalar and rejects every Rust proof; \code{verify_iff_compiled} is then false. The fix that keeps the spine's statements: give the stack the inner-product oracle interface (a query is a \code{Weight μ}, the answer \code{Σ_w W(w)·q(w)}, the idealization of Definition 3.13); the opening phase is then ``\code{λ}, then one weighted query'', a one-challenge component, and WHIR realizes that one query (typechecked against ArkLib at the pin, probe \code{InnerProductOracle}). \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile A.1 to A.5 (recommendation (ii)); brief §7.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.2}\textbf{2.3.5.2 Perfect completeness.} \emph{States:} by linearity of \code{Weight.pair}, the batched claim holds of \code{q} when every pooled claim does. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.3}\textbf{2.3.5.3 Knowledge soundness} (\lean{openingPhase_rbrKnowledgeSoundness}, \code{bp:1114}). \emph{States:} before \code{λ} ``some pooled claim is false of \code{q}''; after \code{λ} ``the batched claim is false of \code{q}'', error \code{(J − 1)/|E|} on \code{λ} (a nonzero polynomial of degree below \code{J}); the one query makes the verdict. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; the blueprint's ``\code{2/|E|} per round'' is the tail's value of Theorem B.7 and belongs to no round of this phase. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile A.5 (table, Layer 10 row), B.6.
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.3.1}\textbf{2.3.5.3.1 A column claim is a weighted claim} (\lean{ColumnClaim.holds_iff_weighted}, \code{ClaimWeights.lean:58}; \lean{eqWeight}, \lean{eqWeight_pair}, \lean{Weight.pair_eq_sumCube}). \emph{States:} a claim on column \code{c} at \code{z} is the weighted claim with weight \code{eq(extend c z, ·)}; the strided limb claims need the strided extension (2.5.6.3). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (probe \code{ValuesProbe}). \emph{See:} code-layer1 A.7, B.7.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.3.2}\textbf{2.3.5.3.2 The pool's order and the assignment of the powers of \code{λ}.} \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} (convention \emph{Claim pool order}, \code{bp:324}); agrees with the three sources. \emph{See:} gt-opening-compile A.2, A.6; gt-flock-ring negative results.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.3.3}\textbf{2.3.5.3.3 The batching component} (2.5.2).
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.3.5.4}\textbf{2.3.5.4 \code{Seam.done} is \code{True}.} \emph{States:} the last phase leaves nothing to check; the opening's knowledge soundness therefore says ``if the verifier accepts, every pooled claim holds of \code{q} except with the error''. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition} (\code{Seam.done = Set.univ}, probe of code-spine E.2).
\end{itemize}

\subsection[The generic components (2.5)]{The generic components and the layers below the phases (2.5)}\label{sec:obl-tier-generic}


\subsubsection{Sumcheck for eq-weighted virtual polynomials (2.5.1; Layer 4, holes G1 and G2)}\label{sec:obl-gen-sumcheck}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.5.1.1 Definition} (\lean{Virtual}, \lean{sumcheck}, \code{bp:880-893}). \emph{States:} \code{n} rounds, each a round polynomial of degree \code{d} sent as \code{d + 1} coefficients and a challenge, then the claimed table values at the point; the output relation says each value is the table's extension at the point and the formula reproduces the running claim. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{missing} — two variants are needed and only the plain one is defined: the normalized (Gruen) variant, whose round message is the cofactor of degree \code{d} with \code{c_0} derived through the equality factor and no equality factor in the final check, is the one the GKR runs; the table sumcheck sends three of four coefficients with \code{c_1} derived. \emph{See:} gt-bus G1 (GB1); gt-table-pub A.1 (T5, T6).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.2}\textbf{2.5.1.2 Perfect completeness} (\lean{sumcheck_perfectCompleteness}, \code{bp:894}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; ArkLib's \code{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.reduction_perfectCompleteness} is \oblstatus{major}{admitted upstream} (through the admitted \code{liftContext_perfectCompleteness}), which the blueprint's ledger row A1 omits. \emph{See:} lib-arklib B.3 (row A1).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.3}\textbf{2.5.1.3 Round-by-round knowledge soundness} (\lean{sumcheck_rbrKnowledgeSoundness … (fun _ ↦ d/|F|)}, \code{bp:895-896}). \emph{States:} if the running claim is false before a round, the prover's message differs from the true round polynomial and the two agree at most at \code{d} points. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; ArkLib's \code{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.verifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} and its lens instances \oblstatus{major}{admitted upstream} at both pins (ledger A1). \emph{See:} lib-arklib B.3, F.1.
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.3.1}\textbf{2.5.1.3.1 Two distinct polynomials of degree at most \code{d} agree at most at \code{d} points} (Mathlib \lean{Polynomial.card_roots'}, \lean{Polynomial.eq_of_degree_le_of_eval_finset_eq}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin}. \emph{See:} \code{bp:275-277}.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.3.2}\textbf{2.5.1.3.2 The uniform sampler's counting bound} (2.3.3.3.3).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.3.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.5.1.3.3 The round identity as derivation} (the wire drops one coefficient; the verifier derives it from the running claim). \emph{States:} the dropped-coefficient encoding is inverted by the running claim, so a protocol that sends all coefficients and checks the identity accepts the same transcripts as one that derives; Fiat–Shamir absorbs different data, so a transport lemma is owed. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing}. \emph{See:} gt-table-pub finding ``the round message'' (TP4); gt-bus B (B15).
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.1.4}\textbf{2.5.1.4 The eq-weighted, back-loaded variant} (\code{bp:898-904}). \emph{States:} tables of different heights lifted by \code{∏_{k ≥ τ_j} X_k} (\code{sumCube_prodVars}, \code{sumCube_padHigh}), the verifier's running weight \code{∏} of the challenges a table sat out, \code{eq(ζ_{<τ_j}, ·)} as an explicit factor evaluated by the verifier. \emph{Status:} the Layer 1 identities \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (\code{Padding.lean:47, 64, 70}); the variant \oblstatus{note}{specified only}. \emph{See:} code-layer1 A.6, B.4.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Batching by the powers of one challenge (2.5.2; Layer 4, hole G3)}\label{sec:obl-gen-batching}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.2.1}\textbf{2.5.2.1 Definition and knowledge soundness} (\lean{batchClaims}, \lean{batchClaims_rbrKnowledgeSoundness … (k − 1)/|F|}, \code{bp:907-911}). \emph{States:} the invariant ``some claim is false''; escape needs the batching polynomial, of degree below \code{k}, to vanish at the challenge. \emph{Feeds:} 2.3.2.4 (\code{ξ}), 2.3.5.3 (\code{λ}), the GKR's combiners, WHIR's per-level batching. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; ArkLib \#615's \code{gammaPowers} is a pattern. \emph{See:} gt-table-pub D.2 (the argument, worked).
