\subsubsection{Fingerprints and the grand product (2.5.3; Layer 5, hole G4)}\label{sec:obl-gen-fingerprint}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.3.1}\textbf{2.5.3.1 The fingerprint and the side product} (\lean{fingerprint}, \lean{sideProduct}, \code{bp:923-924}). \emph{States:} \code{π_α(t) = Σ_{i<16} eq(α, bits i)·t_i} with \code{α ∈ E^4}; the product over the multiset of \code{β − π_α(t)}; padding leaves are \code{1}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition} for the bit order (\code{bitProductTable}, \code{lagrangeBasis}).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.3.2}\textbf{2.5.3.2 The product polynomial determines the multiset} (\lean{sideProduct_poly_eq_iff}, Lemma 5.2, \code{bp:926-928}). \emph{States:} in \code{K[A_0, …, A_3, X]} the products of the monic linear factors \code{X − π_A(t)} agree iff the multisets do (unique factorization; monic factors are equal, not merely associate; \code{t ↦ π_A(t)} injective). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; Mathlib's \code{UniqueFactorizationMonoid} on \code{MvPolynomial} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin}; the specification's proof is \code{TODO}. \emph{See:} gt-bus E.2; \code{bp:278-279}.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.3.3}\textbf{2.5.3.3 The collision bound} (\lean{sideProduct_collision}, Theorem 5.1, \code{bp:929-931}). \emph{States:} unequal multisets of size at most \code{2^μ} collide at \code{(α, β)} with probability at most \code{4·2^μ/|E|} (total degree \code{4N}, \code{N ≤ 2^μ}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; Schwartz–Zippel \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin} (ArkLib \code{schwartz_zippel_counting} in the root namespace, \code{prob_eval_zero_le_div} a \code{PMF} statement: the blueprint's names are wrong). \emph{See:} lib-arklib G.6 (AK6); acceptance test 1.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The batched radix-4 GKR (2.5.4; Layer 5, holes G5 and G6)}\label{sec:obl-gen-gkr}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.4.1}\oblflag\textbf{2.5.4.1 Definition} (\lean{ProductTree}, \lean{gkr nside μ}, \lean{gkrError}, \code{bp:933-944}). \emph{States:} from the roots to the leaf claims: radix 4 from the root down, one radix-2 layer first if \code{μ} is odd; a combiner after the roots and after every layer (the last unused); per layer \code{k = μ − layer} normalized sumcheck rounds of degree 4, twelve children, the layer check \code{claim = Σ_s λ^s ∏ children[s]} with no equality factor, two combination challenges; the three trees share every challenge and end at one \code{ζ}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only} \oblreview{wrong} (degree 5, one combiner per layer, no binary-layer error; 2.3.1.3.4). \emph{See:} gt-bus A.4, D.4, G1, G2, G12.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.4.2}\textbf{2.5.4.2 Perfect completeness} (\lean{gkr_perfectCompleteness}, \code{bp:942}). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; an honest GKR prover written from the specification is accepted by the pinned Python verifier (gt-bus probe H.1).
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.4.3}\textbf{2.5.4.3 Round-by-round knowledge soundness} (\lean{gkr_rbrKnowledgeSoundness … (gkrError nside μ)}, \code{bp:943-944}). \emph{States:} per challenge as in 2.3.1.3.4; the layer check turns a false running claim into a false child. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; the specification states no error for the GKR (gt-bus G17). Its leaves: the sumcheck of 2.5.1 in its normalized variant; the batching of 2.5.2 for the combiners; the bilinear interpolation of the four children (\code{1/|E|} per coordinate).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The ring-switching and WHIR components (2.5.5)}\label{sec:obl-gen-rs-whir}

Ring switching is 2.3.4.3.5 (inside the Flock phase, \#3's); WHIR is 2.1.2.4 (Layer 11, the compilation). Neither is a phase of the oracle protocol; under recommendation (ii) the opening phase is the batching component alone.


\subsubsection[Layer 1 (2.5.6)]{Layer 1 (2.5.6): hypercube tables, stacking, padding, claim weights, the fixed columns (built)}\label{sec:obl-gen-layer1}

Every theorem below is \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} (seventeen declarations checked with \texttt{\#print axioms} by code-layer1, three standard axioms; the sketch matches the code declaration by declaration). Today an auditor of the master theorems reads none of them; seventeen definitions become trusted when the adaptor is built, about eight more with the executable verifier (code-layer1 E).

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.6.1}\textbf{2.5.6.1 The generic identities} (\code{ToCompPoly/}; over any commutative ring). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} for each of the following.
\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \textendash\enspace \code{evalMle_eq_sumCube_hadamard}, \code{sumCube_lagrangeBasis} (partition of unity), \code{evalMle_replicate}, \code{evalMle_lagrangeBasis} (the eq kernel; duplicates CompPoly's \code{eqTilde_eq_prod}) — \code{Multilinear.lean:91, 125, 131}, \code{BitProductTable.lean:156}.
\item \textendash\enspace \code{evalMle_append_boolVec} (\code{Multilinear.lean:342}): the extension at \code{(z, bits of j)} is the extension of slice \code{j} at \code{z} (high-index selection; the low-index, strided selection is absent: 2.5.6.3). \code{evalMle_placeSlice}, \code{sumCube_placeSlice} (\code{:371, 381}).
\item \textendash\enspace \code{evalMle_bitProductTable}, \code{evalMle_powersTable} (\code{BitProductTable.lean:58, 144}): a table that factors over the index bits evaluates as a product.
\item \textendash\enspace \code{Blocks.pow_size_dvd_offset} (alignment from the order), \code{Blocks.stack_eval} (the one selector fact: \code{q̃(z, sel_b) = P̃_b(z)} for the honest stack), \code{Blocks.unstack_eval₂} (the same for a table the prover chose), \code{Blocks.stack_eval_ambient} (equation (2) of §5.4 for any padding) — \code{Stacking.lean:109, 339, 330}, \code{AmbientStacking.lean:134}.
\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.6.2}\textbf{2.5.6.2 The leanVM half} (\oblstatus{ok}{built and proved} for each). \code{Blocks.readColumn_eval}, \code{Blocks.layout} (the aligned blocks as the spine's \code{Layout}), \code{Layout.comap} (renaming; accepts a non-injective renaming, so a layout built with it can alias), \code{Blocks.stack_eval_ambient_one} (padding \code{1} over \code{E}, the leaf decomposition), \code{sumCube_padHigh}, \code{evalMle_padHigh}, \code{eqWeight}, \code{eqWeight_pair}, \code{ColumnClaim.holds_iff_weighted}, \code{idxColumn_eval}, \code{idxColumnEval_eq} (the index column \code{g^i}, coordinate \code{k} carrying \code{g^{2^k}}, §6.5), \code{bytecodeColumn_answer_boolVec}, \code{bytecodeColumn_eval} (slot \code{s} of instruction \code{z} at \code{(z, s)}, cell for cell the Rust encoder's table on a sixteen-instruction program). \emph{See:} code-layer1 A.5 to A.9, B.1 to B.7.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.6.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.5.6.3 The strided reader of the eighteen BLAKE2S limb columns} (\lean{sliceLow}, \lean{evalMle_boolVec_append}, \lean{Blocks.stridedLayout}, \lean{Layout.piecewise}; no blueprint name). \emph{States:} a limb column is read from \code{q_flock} at the low eight coordinates frozen to the slot's bits; the selection lemma is twenty lines (probe \code{StridedProbe}, proved). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{major}{not specified} \oblreview{missing} — exists nowhere, assigned to no layer; \code{leanIsaInstance} cannot be built without it. \emph{See:} code-layer1 G.1 (L1-1); gt-flock-ring 8.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.6.4}\oblflag\textbf{2.5.6.4 The order of equal-size blocks.} \emph{States:} the six shared columns first, then every table's columns in table order (\code{witness.rs:67-79}, \code{cpu/layout.rs:13-49}); \code{Blocks} is the sorted sizes only, and leanVM's order and ``tables first'' give different offsets with the same \code{Blocks}. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data} \oblreview{missing} — pinned by no statement or test before the compiled verifier. \emph{See:} code-layer1 G.3 (L1-3), B.2 (the 92 offsets of the pinned Python layout reproduced by \code{Blocks.offset}).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection[Layer 0 (2.5.7)]{Layer 0 (2.5.7): the fields, the samplers, the oracle interface (built)}\label{sec:obl-gen-layer0}

\begin{itemize}[label={}, leftmargin=1.3em, itemindent=-1.3em, labelwidth=0pt, labelsep=0pt, itemsep=4pt, topsep=3pt]
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.7.1}\textbf{2.5.7.1 The fields and their cardinality} (\lean{K}, \lean{E}, \lean{card_E : Fintype.card E = 2^192}, \code{Field.lean:96}; CompPoly's \lean{card_ext3}). \emph{States:} \code{K = GF(2)[x]/(x^64+x^4+x^3+x+1)} as 64-bit words, \code{E = K[y]/(y^3+y+1)} as limb triples, bit for bit leanVM's (probe \code{FieldFidelity}: eleven Rust reference products reproduced). \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{library, proved at the old pin} (irreducibility by a Rabin certificate, no \code{native_decide}); at the new pin \code{BF64} is a structure and \code{(2 : K) = 0}. \emph{See:} lib-others B, G.8.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.7.2}\textbf{2.5.7.2 Uniform challenges} (\lean{instSampleableTypeE}, \code{Field.lean:93}; VCVio's \lean{SampleableType}). \emph{States:} uniformity is a law of the class, so the \code{E} sampler (three limbs through a bijection) is uniform by proof; \code{Pr[= x | $ᵗ E] = 2^{-192}} (probe \code{Layer0}); the \code{K} sampler has no consumer. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}. \emph{See:} lib-others E.1, G.2.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.7.3}\oblflag\textbf{2.5.7.3 The evaluation oracle} (\lean{evalOracle}, \lean{evalOracle_answer}, \code{Field.lean:102-113}). \emph{States:} a query is a point of \code{E^n}, the answer \code{q̃(r) = Σ_i ofK(q_i)·eq(r, i)} in the specification's little-endian order. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built and proved}; \oblreview{wrong} as the interface of the stack: the compilation needs the inner-product interface (2.3.5.1), of which evaluation is the case \code{W = eq(r, ·)}. \emph{See:} lib-others E.2; gt-opening-compile A.5.
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.5.7.4}\textbf{2.5.7.4 The scalar oracle interfaces} (\lean{instOracleInterfaceE}, \lean{instOracleInterfaceListE}, \code{Field.lean:115-118}). \emph{States:} a scalar or list message is read whole. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{ok}{built, definition} \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, transcribed data}, unlisted in the blueprint's interface list. \emph{See:} lib-others G.4 (LO4).
\end{itemize}

The only place the proof system meets leanISA. Nothing of it exists in Lean at \code{b435631} (\code{M3Holds}, \code{M3Rel} and \code{Refinement} are built; \code{leanIsaInstance}, \code{stackOf}, \code{witnessOf} and the four theorems are not).

\end{itemize}
\item \phantomsection\label{obl:node-2.6.3}\textbf{2.6.3 The completeness bridge} (\lean{m3Holds_stackOf (h : SatisfiedBy prog input w) (hs : Sizes.ofWitness w = some s) : M3Holds (leanIsaInstance prog s) input (stackOf gen w hs)}, \code{bp:817-818}). \emph{States:} the stack of a satisfying witness (with the Flock wires generated from the limbs) satisfies \code{M3Holds}; the non-vacuity of the whole protocol for leanISA. \emph{Feeds:} 2.0.2. \emph{Status:} \oblstatus{note}{specified only}; needs \code{Sizes.ofWitness} (ill-defined while \code{Sizes} holds \code{logInvRate}) and \code{FlockWitnessGen} with its lemma ``the generated wires satisfy the R1CS when the limbs compress'' \oblstatus{minor}{trusted, assumed interface} (\#3's). \emph{See:} boundary-adaptor A.6, C; gt-flock-ring 7.1 (row 3).

\subsection{The non-interactive error}\label{sec:obl-error-ni}

\textbf{As the blueprint writes it} (\code{bp:1224}, \code{bp:1234-1235}):
\[
  \mathit{niError} = Q \cdot \max_i \varepsilon_i
\]
``plus the grinding-adjusted WHIR terms''.

\textbf{What the review finds it must be}, per random-oracle query, for a $t$-query adversary
against \code{verify^H} with $k$ rounds:
\begin{align*}
  \mathit{niError}(t) ={}& (t + k)\cdot\max\Bigl( L_0\cdot\max_{\text{front}}\varepsilon_i,\;
     \max_{\text{fold}}\frac{2L_i + 2^{\ell_i - j}a_i}{\abs{\E}},\;
     \max_{\text{query}} 2^{-b_i}(1 - \gamma_i)^{t_i},\\
  &\hphantom{(t + k)\cdot\max\Bigl(}\text{the OOD, batching, final and tail terms}\Bigr)\\
  &+ \frac{3.5\,t^2}{2^{256}} \qquad \text{(the hash chain and the Merkle trees)}\\
  &+ \text{the program-hash collision term},
\end{align*}
uniform in the announced sizes $s$ or maximized over them, with the multiplier $(t + k)$ of
[CY24] Theorems 31.2.1/31.3.1 (or $Q$ of [BGKTTZ23] Theorem 3.15), the list factor $L_0$ on every
challenge of the oracle protocol (they precede the point where the claims pin one list member),
the grinding bits $b_i = 17$ at every query round as a per-round multiplicative factor (an
assumption no published theorem covers), and the hash term that caps a 256-bit digest at the
edge of 128 bits of average-case security.

\textbf{The terms the blueprint's formula lacks}:
\begin{itemize}
\item the list-size factor $L_0$ (literature LT2; gt-flock-ring FR13);
\item the hash-collision term (LT3);
\item a model of grinding (LT1: without it the formula certifies about 111 bits where leanVM
  claims 128);
\item the family composition over the prover's sizes (boundary-adaptor finding 6);
\item the program-hash collision (gt-opening-compile E.1).
\end{itemize}
The maximum is set by the query rounds ($2^{-111}\cdot 2^{-17} = 2^{-128}$) and the folds
($2^{-128.2}$), not by anything in the oracle protocol; the theorem is classical (no quantum
random-oracle model, LT14).

\textbf{Which theorems carry which term.} \lean{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} carries the front's
$\varepsilon_i$ per challenge (2.2.2); the list-binding compilation multiplies them by $L_0$ and
adds Theorem B.7's (2.1.2.3, 2.1.2.4); the round-by-round to state-restoration step gives the
$(t + k)$ multiplier (2.1.2.1.1); the Merkle interface adds the hash term (2.1.2.2); the chain
lemma adds the encoding collision (2.1.2.1.2); the grinding model turns $b_i$ into $2^{-b_i}$
(2.1.2.1.3); the family composition handles $s$ (2.1.2.1.6). Of these seven steps, one is built
(the first), one is admitted upstream in a weaker form (the third), and five are stated
nowhere. \Cref{tab:obl-arrows} sets the same steps against the arrows of the dossier's summary
(\cref{sec:obl-shape}).

\section{Findings from the tree}\label{sec:obl-findings}

Only what the tree reveals and no sibling dossier states as such; each finding cites the nodes it rests on. The severities are the brief's.

\begin{finding}{major}{f:obl-unowned}{Twenty-one obligations of the composition have no hole, no layer and no owner}
\fhead{Evidence} The closing list of \cref{sec:obl-holes} against the holes table (\code{bp:594-617}) and the layers (\code{bp:619-1259}): each item is needed by an arrow of the chain in section 2 and appears in no hole's ``Produces'' column and in no layer's sketch. Sibling dossiers record most of them one at a time (gt-opening-compile E.2, E.3; literature A.4; code-layer1 G.1; boundary-adaptor findings 2, 6, 7; gt-bus G7, G10; gt-table-pub TP1, TP4; code-spine CS1); none states that the plan's unit of work leaves them unassigned.

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (the plan is incomplete, not wrong where it is stated).

\fhead{Proposed change} Add to the holes table one row per item, or fold them into the nearest hole's ``Produces'' column: the transcript hole (K3) gains the Merkle compilation, the chain lemma, the state-restoration step, the grinding model, the hash and program-hash terms, the family composition, the canonical-encoding checks; the WHIR hole (K1) gains the \code{K}-valuedness lemma and \code{encode} over \code{E}; a new hole ``list-binding compilation'' (between the WHIR hole and the transcript hole) gains 2.1.2.3 with its union-bound lemma and the oracle-freeness requirement; the Layer 1 hole (L1) gains the strided reader and the tie order; the hole of Clean components as polynomials (I1) gains the boundary-block bridge and the count columns; the adaptor (I2) gains the carrier of ``R1CS \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} compress''; the public-input hole (P5) gains the deployed phase; the sumcheck hole (G1) gains the normalized variant and the dropped-coefficient transport; the spine (S) gains the bound on \code{piopError}.

\fhead{Reason} A reader of the holes table today believes that filling twenty-two units yields \code{baseVerifier_extractsExecution}; it yields the two master theorems and a \code{verify} with no theorem tying them together.

\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{major}{f:obl-oracle-free-front}{The compilation needs every phase before the opening to make no oracle query, and nothing states or enforces it}
\fhead{Evidence} The list-binding compilation (2.1.2.3, gt-opening-compile E.3) replaces the commit message by a codeword and keeps the front's verifier unchanged; that is possible only if the front's verifier never queries the stack, since a query answered by \code{q̃} has no counterpart when the oracle is a word close to a list. The two built phases do not query (the commit verifier reads nothing; the public-input verifier queries only its own message, \code{PublicInput.lean:222-231}). The spine's \code{Phase.Def} allows a verifier to query the stack at any point any number of times (ArkLib's \code{OracleVerifier}; neither ArkLib nor the spine counts queries, \code{OracleVerifier.numQueries} being \code{sorry}), and code-spine D.3 (d) and gt-table-pub E.4 item 6 show that a phase reading the whole stack fills every slot. So a bundle \code{Phases I} may satisfy both master theorems and be uncompilable. Under the blueprint's evaluation interface the opening phase itself queries once (the final evaluation), so the requirement is ``every phase but the last''; under recommendation (ii) it is ``every phase but the opening's one weighted query, which WHIR realizes''. No sentence of the blueprint, the tracker or the spine's docstrings states it.

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (an omission in the design of the seams).

\fhead{Proposed change} Either a field of \code{Phases} (or a hypothesis of the compilation theorem) ``the verifier of each front phase makes no query to \code{TheOracle I}'', stated as a property of the \code{OracleVerifier} (its \code{verify} computation is in the image of the query-free embedding), with the two built phases as its first inhabitants; or a stronger type for the front phases, an \code{OracleReduction} whose verifier is a plain \code{Verifier} over \code{[]ₒ} lifted by \code{keepOracles}, so that a query is a typing error. Add to the conventions row \emph{The oracle} (\code{bp:317}): ``No phase before the opening queries it; the opening queries it once (under (ii)); the compilation depends on this.''

\fhead{Reason} Without it the sentence ``WHIR realizes the oracle'' has no theorem behind it for an arbitrary bundle, and a phase written in the ideal model with a convenient query would pass every planned check and break the compilation.

\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{minor}{f:obl-grinding}{The per-challenge error has no carrier for the grinding bits, and the compiled protocol's schedule must carry them}
\fhead{Evidence} \code{Component.Def.err : pSpec.ChallengeIdx → ℝ≥0} (\code{Component.lean:66}) is what \code{piopError} sums and what the Fiat–Shamir interface consumes (\code{bp:1224}: ``error \code{Q · max_i ε_i}''); leanVM's 128-bit claim needs, per challenge, both \code{ε_i} and the grinding bits \code{b_i} (2.1.2.1.3; literature A.3 item 3). The ground rounds are WHIR's query rounds only, which live in the compiled protocol (2.1.2.4.7), not in the oracle protocol, so the spine's \code{err} is the right type for the front; but \code{leanVmIopp}'s definition (2.1.3) must expose \code{b_i} per challenge and the Fiat–Shamir interface must take it. The blueprint's \code{niError} prose (``grinding-adjusted WHIR terms'') names no such datum.

\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (an omission in the data of Layer 12).

\fhead{Proposed change} Give the compiled reduction's definition a second function \code{grind : pSpec.ChallengeIdx → ℕ} (zero everywhere but at the query rounds, \code{17} there), make \code{FiatShamirSecurity} take it, and define \code{niError} from \code{err} and \code{grind}.

\fhead{Reason} The statement of the interface must be able to say which challenge is ground.

\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{note}{f:obl-smallest-set}{The two master theorems are conditional on bundles no instance but the toy can inhabit today, and the tree shows the smallest set of nodes that makes them about leanVM}
\fhead{Evidence} Reading the tree bottom-up from \code{piop_perfectCompleteness} and \code{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (2.2.1, 2.2.2), the nodes that must exist for the theorems to be about leanVM's verifier, and are not built, are: the instance (2.6.1, with 2.5.6.3, 2.5.8), the four unbuilt phases' \code{Def}s (2.3.1.1, 2.3.2.1, 2.3.4.1, 2.3.5.1), their \code{Complete} and \code{Security} (eight fields), the bound 2.2.2.5, the non-vacuity theorem 2.6.3, and the refinement 2.1.1 with its fixture. That is the whole of Layers 3, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12's \code{verify_iff_compiled}; nothing smaller pins the phases (2.2.2.6). Every other node of the tree is above (the compilation's security) or below (the generic components, whose theorems the phases' proofs consume).

\fhead{Classification} Not a divergence; a reading aid for the report's chapter.

\fhead{Proposed change} None to the blueprint beyond \cref{f:obl-unowned}; the status file should list these nodes as ``what makes the master theorems about leanVM'' separately from the holes.

\end{finding}

\paragraph{Negative results.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Every node of the blueprint's Layers 0 to 13 and of its holes table has a place in the tree; no blueprint obligation was found redundant (every layer feeds \code{verify} or a theorem about it; agrees with boundary-adaptor F). Three named declarations serve nothing on the chain (\code{witnessOf_stackOf}, \code{Extractor.Straightline.map}, \code{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness_exists}): non-vacuity tests or upstream candidates, as boundary-adaptor F says.
\item The per-challenge errors of the built phase (\code{1/|E|}) and of the two sketched phases whose arguments the sibling dossiers worked (table: \code{(B+2)/|E|} on \code{ξ}, \code{3/|E|} per round; opening: \code{(J−1)/|E|} on \code{λ}) are correct and tight, on the right challenges (gt-table-pub D; code-pubinput F; gt-opening-compile A.5). The bus phase's \code{(α, β)} term is correct within a factor 2.
\item The composition of errors through the spine is per challenge with no additive term (lib-arklib G.9, \code{KnowledgeAppend.lean} read in full by that dossier); \cref{sec:obl-error-interactive} adds nothing at the seams.
\item The hypotheses table (\cref{tab:obl-hypotheses}) reproduces boundary-adaptor C's rows and adds six (the grinding check, the canonical encodings, \code{R1CS_DIGEST}, the \code{F_2}-independence of the fixed weights, the oracle-freeness of the front, the bound on \code{piopError}); none of boundary-adaptor's rows was found wrong.
\end{itemize}
